body:
This is the line where Webpack crashes:

![](https://www.dropbox.com/s/k3t8fnu37zhj4hv/Screen%20Shot%202016-04-25%20at%2018.21.00.png?raw=1)
Have you had a change to give Webpack 2 a try? It might be fixed there, but I haven’t checked.
I'll try and see if I can work out how to upgrade now

It builds fine with Webpack 2 without any change in config.

HRM isn't working with it at all though. It claims to be, and doesn't error, but I'm getting no actual changes. I think I'll wait on Webpack 2 until there's some more documentation around it.

![](https://www.dropbox.com/s/izehy84w9wybbl8/Screen%20Shot%202016-04-27%20at%2020.59.33.png?raw=1)

Just wanted to chime in that I have been observing this same issue for about a year now. Webpack 1. I have yet to discover a pattern. The bad thing is that after this has occurred, HMR seems no longer functional so we have to restart the app.

It would be great if there at least would be a guard added so that HMR doesn't crash.
This might have been fixed in webpack 2 since there were quite a few hot reloading changes around June or so.

Could we maybe add some diagnostics code? Because upgrading to Webpack 2 is a big time investment and at the moment still very risky.

I understand that it will be very difficult to fix from the current info, but the message clearly indicates that the HMR runtime is in a state it should never be in. The `module.parents` array apparently contains an ID of a module that is no longer found in `installedModules`. Might this happen when we remove an `import` / `require` statement? 

Maybe we can just test whether `parent` is `undefined` and if it is, log some debug info (so next time someone encounters it they'll have more info for us) and `continue` to the next loop iteration. That seems like a safe change to make that may help alleviate and finally fix this issue.

body:
I am encountering the same sporadically when hot reloading my server.

I think this may be the culprit: https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/028c51301733836abbedc88be7483af2623f5943/lib/HotModuleReplacement.runtime.js#L502

in all the other places `module` is guarded against being undefined but here apparently not?

error is:
```
[HMR] Update failed: TypeError: Cannot read property 'hot' of undefined
    at hotApply (/.../build/server/webpack:/webpack/bootstrap 7bade06584d268e6755d:520:1)
    at hotUpdateDownloaded (/.../build/server/webpack:/webpack/bootstrap 7bade06584d268e6755d:245:1)
    at hotAddUpdateChunk (/.../build/server/webpack:/webpack/bootstrap 7bade06584d268e6755d:225:1)
    at hotDownloadUpdateChunk (/.../build/server/webpack:/webpack/bootstrap 7bade06584d268e6755d:3:1)
    at hotEnsureUpdateChunk (/.../build/server/webpack:/webpack/bootstrap 7bade06584d268e6755d:235:1)
    at /.../build/server/webpack:/webpack/bootstrap 7bade06584d268e6755d:206:1
```
(.../build/server is the outputDir)

Having exactly same issue on Webpack 2, which kills my SCSS hot module replacement. Happens each time I'm trying to apply new SCSS changes.

Update:

Spiked (fixed) issue by wrapping `// call accept handlers` code  (L497 - L532) into `try/catch` block in file `./node_modules/webpack/lib/HotModuleReplacement.runtime.js`

I am using webpack 3 and still having the same error when running webpack dev server. Any update on this?

cheers,
Khoa

```
manifest.js:590 Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'hot' of undefined
    at hotApply (manifest.js:590)
    at hotUpdateDownloaded (manifest.js:314)
    at hotAddUpdateChunk (manifest.js:294)
    at webpackHotUpdateCallback (manifest.js:37)
    at 0.a0cbf6c….hot-update.js:1
```

I‘m using webpack3 + vue-loader through webpack nodejs api.

when I modify the `template` tag in the `.vue` file, hmr worked fine.
moduleId `./App.vue` was in the installedModules array

but if I modify the code in the `script` tag, the error above was thrown,
and moduleId `./App.vue` was gone.

In my `dev.config.js` file, I added `hmr: ['webpack/hot/dev-server', 'webpack-dev-server/client?http://localhost:8080']` into the entry field, and `new webpack.HotModuleReplacementPlugin()` into the plugins array, also, `hot: true` was in the `webpackDevServer`'s second arguments as well

I tried CLI to run webpack-dev-server with `--hot --inline`, both `template` tag and `script` tag work fine.

I've been having the same issue (version 2.6.1). I'm using Vue with vue-loader and it happens only on certain components when editing the contents of the script tag.
Don't know if this is a vue-loader or a general webpack issue.

The error comes from ``HotModuleReplacement.runtime.js`` line 500, because ``installedModules[moduleId]`` doesn't exist.
